title: Bank Holidays: Plan Transactions for May 25-31 Closures
description: Banks across various states in India will observe specific holidays between May 25 and May 31, 2024. A significant pan-India bank holiday is scheduled for May.

faq.q: Are all banks closed on the same days?
faq.a: No, not all banks close on the exact same days across India. While national holidays like Bakrid (May 27) are widely observed, many bank holidays are state-specific, depending on local festivals and observances. Always check the RBI's holiday list for your specific region.

faq.q: Can I use UPI or net banking during a bank holiday?
faq.a: Yes, absolutely. Digital banking services like UPI, NEFT, RTGS, internet banking, and mobile banking applications operate 24x7, 365 days a year, including on bank holidays. You can perform fund transfers, bill payments, and other transactions digitally.

faq.q: What if I need to deposit a cheque?
faq.a: Physical cheque deposits require a bank branch to be open. If you have an urgent cheque deposit, ensure you do it on a working day before the holiday. Cheque clearing will only commence on the next working day after the holiday. For urgent fund transfers, consider NEFT or RTGS.

faq.q: How do I find the exact bank holidays for my state?
faq.a: The most reliable source is the official Reserve Bank of India (RBI) website (https://rbi.org.in), which publishes a comprehensive list of bank holidays categorised by state. Your bank's official website also typically lists the holidays applicable to its branches.

faq.q: Do bank holidays affect stock market trading?
faq.a: Bank holidays generally do not affect stock market trading unless the holiday falls on a day when the stock exchanges (NSE and BSE) are also officially closed. Stock market holidays are declared separately by SEBI and the exchanges, often coinciding with major public holidays.

faq.q: Will my EMI payments be debited on a bank holiday?
faq.a: If your EMI payment is set up via an auto-debit mandate, it will typically be processed on the due date, even if it's a bank holiday. However, if the due date falls on a bank holiday and the processing system requires a working day, the debit might occur on the next working day. Ensure sufficient funds are available.
